title: Understanding the Problem
text: To find the optimal value of theta using mean square error, we need to understand that theta represents the predicted values for each color. The goal is to minimize the difference between the predicted values and the actual values.

title: Mean Square Error Formula
text: The mean square error (MSE) is calculated as the average of the squares of the differences between the predicted values and the actual values. The formula is: $$MSE=\frac{\sum \left(y_{pred}-y_{actual}\right)^2}{n}$$, where $$y_{pred}$$ is the predicted value, $$y_{actual}$$ is the actual value, and $$n$$ is the number of data points.

title: Identifying the Predicted Values
text: In this problem, the predicted values (theta) should match the actual values to minimize the mean square error. Therefore, the optimal theta is the same as the actual values given in the problem.
